instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a 'lobbyist' as an individual who receives 'economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses,' from a principal and whose duties include lobbying, without setting any minimum dollar amount of compensation.

A principal must register only after exceeding $500 in aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year (§ 13.64(1)), and principals anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and are exempt from licensing/registration/reporting (§ 13.621(5)).

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled provisions define 'lobbyist' based on receiving economic consideration and/or making lobbying communications on at least 5 days, but do not define any lobbyist-registration trigger based on the lobbyist’s own lobbying expenditures.

The bundled text requires principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements under § 13.68, and lobbyists only provide supporting information to principals (§ 13.68(4)); it does not establish a lobbyist-side expenditure reporting threshold.

The statute includes a 10-hours-per-reporting-period exclusion for certain non-lobbyist employees in principal reporting (§ 13.68(1)(a),(c)), but it does not create any exemption keyed to a percentage of an individual’s compensated time devoted to lobbying.
